problems.title: DRAM speed of light
problems.statement: A GW-1 kernel moves 400 MB of DRAM traffic in 1.0 ms (1.5 million cycles). Peak: 341.3 bytes per cycle.
hints: Bytes / peak bytes per cycle / cycles.

problems.title: Sectors per request
problems.statement: A kernel's global loads: 2,000,000 warp load instructions, 32,000,000 sectors.
problems.solution: 16 sectors per request: 4× the ideal, 25% efficiency. Look for a stride of 4 (or a 16-byte struct read field by field).

problems.title: Issue speed of light
problems.statement: The busiest SM issues 1,200,000 warp instructions in a 1.0 ms kernel (1.5 M cycles), at one per cycle peak.

parts.prompt: Of those, 300,000 are FMAs. FMA share, in %?

problems.solution: 80% issue SOL, but only a quarter is math: issue-bound on overhead (loads, address arithmetic, branches, conflicts), not compute-bound.

problems.title: Intensity from counters
problems.statement: Counters: 3.0 GFLOP, 1.5 GB of DRAM traffic, 2.0 ms on the GW-1.
problems.solution: I = 2, achieved 1,500 GFLOP/s, but the roofline allows only 1,024 at I = 2. A measurement above the roof means a counter is wrong: here, DRAM traffic must be lower than 1.5 GB (cache hits), or the time is wrong. Sanity-check counters against bounds.

problems.title: L2 hit rate and DRAM

parts.prompt: L2 SOL if the kernel took 1.0 ms (683 B/cycle peak), in %?

problems.solution: (a) 75%. (b) 78%: L2 nearly saturated, DRAM at about 39%. This kernel is L2-bound; more DRAM bandwidth wouldn't help.

problems.title: Stall reasons
problems.statement: Match the dominant stall reason to its likely cause.

options: Compute-bound: the math units are full

problems.solution: Long scoreboard: memory. MIO/short scoreboard: shared memory or special functions. Math pipe throttle: the compute units are the bottleneck, which is usually good news.

problems.title: Achieved occupancy
problems.statement: Theoretical occupancy is 100%, but achieved occupancy is 45%.

options: Tail effect: SMs idle at the end of the grid
Imbalanced blocks finishing at different times
Too few blocks for the GPU

problems.solution: Achieved < theoretical means slots exist but aren't filled over time: tails, imbalance or too few blocks. Register limits would lower the theoretical figure itself.

problems.title: Which unit first?
hints: Busiest unit, then split issue by FMA share.
problems.solution: Issue is the busiest unit and mostly FMAs: compute-bound. Next step: tensor cores or lower precision, not memory work.

problems.title: Instructions per element
problems.statement: An elementwise kernel over $2^{24}$ floats issues $4.2 \times 10^6$ warp instructions in total.

parts.prompt: Warp instructions per warp of 32 elements?
If the work is one load, one FMA and one store per element, the ideal?

problems.solution: (a) 8.0 per warp-element group, against (b) 3 ideal: about 5 extra instructions of index arithmetic and loop overhead per element. For a memory-bound kernel that's fine; if issue SOL were high it'd be worth vector loads and a grid-stride loop.

problems.title: Reading Nsight Compute first
hints: What is this kernel using up?
problems.solution: Speed of Light: which unit is near its peak. Then the section for that unit. Starting from source counters is how afternoons disappear.
